subject.title: [Feature]: Script to restore session history archived by new daily-reset mechanism (introduced v2026.2+)

question: Should OpenClaw solve reset archive recovery through read-only family history only, a Doctor-owned restore/re-index command, or both?
rationale: The choice affects transcript mutation, session identity, retention, and exposure of sensitive archived history, so automation should not choose the permanent recovery boundary.

options.title: Land Read-Only Family History First
options.body: Use an explicit, bounded family-history selector as the supported retrieval path before adding archive mutation.

options.title: Add Doctor-Owned Restore/Re-Index
options.body: Create a deliberate recovery command for affected users that preserves source metadata and explains retention and security consequences.

options.title: Reject Mutation-Style Restore
options.body: Keep reset archives read-only and track only discovery, export, and history-reading surfaces.

recommendation.title: Land Read-Only Family History First
recommendation.body: Use an explicit, bounded family-history selector as the supported retrieval path before adding archive mutation.

likelyOwner.reason: They committed the current reset-archive fallback and are the clearest current routing owner for archive history semantics.
